commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-design
commands.description: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). 1	/**
2	 * Governance Dashboard Router — /admin/governance
3	 * 
4	 * Backend procedures for the 3-panel governance dashboard:
5	 * 
6	 * Panel 1: Transport Health

8	 *   - Transport metrics (success rate, latency p50/p95/p99, failures)

16	 *

20	 *   - Active approval tokens
21	 *   - Header injection stats
22	 */

35	// ============================================================================
36	// PANEL 1: TRANSPORT HEALTH

39	const transportHealthProcedure = adminProcedure.query(async () => {

42	  const externalHealth = getExternalGravitoHealth();
43	  const syncMetrics = getSyncWrapperMetrics();
44	
45	  return {
46	    // Current state
47	    transport: {
48	      enabled: status.enabled,
49	      mode: status.mode,

51	      environment: status.environment,
52	      lastError: status.lastError,
53	      lastSuccessAt: status.lastSuccessAt,
54	    },
55	
56	    // Performance metrics
57	    performance: {
58	      totalCalls: metrics.totalCalls,
59	      successCount: metrics.successCount,
60	      failureCount: metrics.failureCount,
61	      successRate: metrics.totalCalls > 0
62	        ? Math.round((metrics.successCount / metrics.totalCalls) * 10000) / 100
63	        : 0,
64	      latency: {
65	        p50: metrics.latencyP50Ms,
66	        p95: metrics.latencyP95Ms,
67	        p99: metrics.latencyP99Ms,
68	      },
69	      transportSwitches: metrics.transportSwitches,
70	    },
71	
72	    // External client health
73	    externalClient: {
74	      circuitBreakerState: externalHealth.circuitBreakerState,
75	      totalCalls: externalHealth.totalCalls,
76	      successRate: externalHealth.successRate,
77	      averageLatencyMs: externalHealth.averageLatencyMs,
78	      fallbackRate: externalHealth.fallbackRate,
79	      lastError: externalHealth.lastError,
80	    },
81	
82	    // Sync wrapper stats
83	    syncWrapper: {
84	      totalSubmissions: syncMetrics.totalSubmissions,
85	      syncResolved: syncMetrics.syncResolved,
86	      asyncReturned: syncMetrics.asyncReturned,
87	      pollAttempts: syncMetrics.pollAttempts,
88	      pollSuccesses: syncMetrics.pollSuccesses,
89	      pollTimeouts: syncMetrics.pollTimeouts,
90	      activeJobs: syncMetrics.activeJobs,
91	    },
92	  };
93	});
94	
95	// ============================================================================
96	// PANEL 2: AUTHORITY DECISIONS
97	// ============================================================================
98	
99	const authorityDecisionsProcedure = adminProcedure
100	  .input(z.object({
101	    days: z.number().min(1).max(90).default(7),
102	    limit: z.number().min(1).max(500).default(50),
103	    surfaceType: z.string().optional(),
104	    regulated: z.boolean().optional(),
105	  }).optional())
106	  .query(async ({ input }) => {
107	    const opts = input || { days: 7, limit: 50 };
108	
109	    // Get authority layer metrics
110	    const authorityMetrics = getAuthorityMetrics();
111	    const authorityHealth = getAuthorityLayerHealth();
112	
113	    // Get inline client metrics
114	    const inlineMetrics = getInlineMetrics();
115	    const breakerState = getCircuitBreakerState();
116	    const uptimeMetrics = getGovernanceUptimeMetrics();
117	
118	    // Get in-memory audit trail (fast)
119	    const memoryAuditTrail = getAuthorityAuditSummary();
120	
121	    // Get database-backed stats (durable)
122	    const dbStats = await getAuthorityAuditStats(opts.days);
123	
124	    // Get recent audit entries from database
125	    const sinceTimestamp = Date.now() - (opts.days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
126	    const recentEntries = await getAuthorityAuditEntries({
127	      limit: opts.limit,
128	      surfaceType: opts.surfaceType,
129	      regulated: opts.regulated,
130	      sinceTimestamp,
131	    });
132	
133	    return {
134	      // Summary statistics
135	      summary: {
136	        totalDecisions: dbStats.totalDecisions,

149	        internalReachable: authorityHealth.internalReachable,
150	        metrics: {
151	          externalSuccesses: authorityMetrics.externalSuccesses,
152	          externalFailures: authorityMetrics.externalFailures,
153	          internalFallbacks: authorityMetrics.internalFallbacks,
154	          failClosedEvents: authorityMetrics.failClosedEvents,
155	          mergedDecisions: authorityMetrics.mergedDecisions,
156	        },
157	      },
158	
159	      // Inline client state
160	      inlineClient: {
161	        circuitBreakerState: breakerState,
162	        totalCalls: inlineMetrics.totalCalls,
163	        successRate: inlineMetrics.successRate,
164	        avgLatencyMs: inlineMetrics.avgLatencyMs,
165	        uptime: uptimeMetrics,
166	      },
167	
168	      // In-memory audit summary
169	      memoryAudit: memoryAuditTrail,
170	
171	      // Recent database entries
172	      recentEntries: recentEntries.map((entry: AuthorityAuditEntry) => ({
173	        id: entry.id,
174	        surfaceType: entry.surfaceType,
175	        regulated: entry.regulated,
176	        externalAttempted: entry.externalAttempted,
177	        externalSuccess: entry.externalSuccess,
178	        mergeStrategy: entry.mergeStrategy,
179	        finalApproved: entry.finalApproved,
180	        finalSeverity: entry.finalSeverity,
181	        totalLatencyMs: entry.totalLatencyMs,
182	        createdAt: entry.createdAt,
183	      })),
184	    };
185	  });
186	
187	// ============================================================================
188	// PANEL 3: REGULATED FLOW
189	// ============================================================================
190	
191	const regulatedFlowProcedure = adminProcedure.query(async () => {
192	  const preApprovalMetrics = getPreApprovalMetrics();
193	  const authorityMetrics = getAuthorityMetrics();
194	
195	  // Get regulated-only audit entries from DB
196	  const regulatedEntries = await getAuthorityAuditEntries({
197	    regulated: true,
198	    limit: 50,
199	    sinceTimestamp: Date.now() - (7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000),
200	  });
201	
202	  return {
203	    // Pre-approval metrics
204	    preApproval: {
205	      requested: preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsRequested,
206	      granted: preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsGranted,
207	      denied: preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsDenied,
208	      failClosed: preApprovalMetrics.failClosedEvents,
209	      approvalRate: preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsRequested > 0
210	        ? Math.round((preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsGranted / preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsRequested) * 10000) / 100
211	        : 0,
212	    },
213	
214	    // Regulated review metrics
215	    regulatedReviews: {
216	      attempted: preApprovalMetrics.regulatedReviewsAttempted,
217	      blocked: preApprovalMetrics.regulatedReviewsBlocked,
218	      blockRate: preApprovalMetrics.regulatedReviewsAttempted > 0
219	        ? Math.round((preApprovalMetrics.regulatedReviewsBlocked / preApprovalMetrics.regulatedReviewsAttempted) * 10000) / 100
220	        : 0,
221	    },
222	
223	    // Header injection stats
224	    headerInjection: {
225	      totalInjected: preApprovalMetrics.headersInjected,
226	      schemaNormalizations: preApprovalMetrics.schemaNormalizations,
227	    },
228	
229	    // Authority layer fail-closed events
230	    failClosed: {
231	      total: authorityMetrics.failClosedEvents,
232	      description: 'Regulated content blocked because external Gravito was unavailable',
233	    },
234	
235	    // Regulated surface types
236	    regulatedSurfaces: Array.from(REGULATED_SURFACES),
237	
238	    // Recent regulated decisions
239	    recentRegulatedDecisions: regulatedEntries.map((entry: AuthorityAuditEntry) => ({
240	      id: entry.id,
241	      surfaceType: entry.surfaceType,
242	      externalAttempted: entry.externalAttempted,
243	      externalSuccess: entry.externalSuccess,
244	      mergeStrategy: entry.mergeStrategy,
245	      finalApproved: entry.finalApproved,
246	      finalSeverity: entry.finalSeverity,
247	      totalLatencyMs: entry.totalLatencyMs,
248	      createdAt: entry.createdAt,
249	    })),
250	  };
251	});
252	
253	// ============================================================================
254	// PROMETHEUS EXPORT
255	// ============================================================================
256	
257	const prometheusExportProcedure = adminProcedure.query(() => {
258	  return {
259	    metrics: exportPrometheusMetrics(),
260	    timestamp: Date.now(),
261	  };
262	});
263	
264	// ============================================================================
265	// COMBINED OVERVIEW (all 3 panels in one call)
266	// ============================================================================
267	
268	const overviewProcedure = adminProcedure
269	  .input(z.object({
270	    days: z.number().min(1).max(90).default(7),
271	  }).optional())
272	  .query(async ({ input }) => {
273	    const days = input?.days || 7;
274	
275	    // Gather all data in parallel
276	    const [
277	      transportStatus,
278	      transportMetrics,
279	      externalHealth,
280	      syncMetrics,
281	      authorityMetrics,
282	      authorityHealth,
283	      preApprovalMetrics,
284	      dbStats,
285	      recentEntries,
286	    ] = await Promise.all([
287	      Promise.resolve(getExternalTransportStatus()),
288	      Promise.resolve(getTransportMetrics()),
289	      Promise.resolve(getExternalGravitoHealth()),
290	      Promise.resolve(getSyncWrapperMetrics()),
291	      Promise.resolve(getAuthorityMetrics()),
292	      Promise.resolve(getAuthorityLayerHealth()),
293	      Promise.resolve(getPreApprovalMetrics()),
294	      getAuthorityAuditStats(days),
295	      getAuthorityAuditEntries({ limit: 20 }),
296	    ]);
297	
298	    return {
299	      // Overall health status
300	      overallHealth: {
301	        status: transportStatus.enabled && authorityHealth.enabled ? 'healthy' :
302	          !transportStatus.enabled && authorityHealth.internalReachable ? 'degraded' :
303	          'critical',
304	        transportMode: transportStatus.mode,
305	        externalReachable: authorityHealth.externalReachable,
306	        internalReachable: authorityHealth.internalReachable,
307	      },
308	
309	      // Key metrics (for dashboard cards)

313	        avgLatencyMs: dbStats.avgLatencyMs,
314	        preApprovalRate: preApprovalMetrics.preApprovalsRequested > 0

316	          : 0,

318	        blockedDecisions: dbStats.blockedDecisions,
319	      },
320

323	        surfaceType: entry.surfaceType,

325	        approved: entry.finalApproved,
326	        latencyMs: entry.totalLatencyMs,
327	        createdAt: entry.createdAt,
328	      })),
329	
330	      periodDays: days,
331	    };

333	
334	// ============================================================================
335	// ROUTER COMPOSITION
336	// ============================================================================
337	
338	export const governanceDashboardRouter = router({
